description: [S7.3, kind `scope`] The app calls TranslateMessage before DispatchMessageW, as every jgld pump does (pumpKeys 0x1006b48c, pumpAll 0x1006b160, pumpChars 0x1006b77c ...: re/analysis/sim/time_input_sites.tsv), so a real key press yields WM_KEYDOWN, WM_CHAR, WM_KEYUP. The corpus traces were recorded with posted messages: the harness posted its own WM_CHAR after each WM_KEYDOWN, and whether jgld's TranslateMessage of that posted WM_KEYDOWN added a second WM_CHAR there is not measured. app_drive.py posts WM_KEYDOWN / WM_KEYUP only (plus one separate WM_CHAR), so in its logs the WM_CHAR after a letter comes from the app's TranslateMessage. Not settled: whether a real keystroke in the original gives exactly one onKey (handler 7) per character, which the live host assumes.
path to resolution: One recording of the original with REAL keystrokes (SendInput on an instance's foreground window, not PostMessage) counting MSG 0x102 records per key press; S7.4's cross-check slot can take it.

description: [S7.3, kind `scope`] The window's client size is MulDiv(800, dpi, 96) x MulDiv(600, dpi, 96) and the presenter replicates logical pixels by floor mapping, so at a non-integer scale (240 dpi = 2.5: 2000 x 1500) columns and rows are 2 or 3 client pixels wide in a fixed pattern. Measured equal to the presenter's mapping and to input_map's to_logical at 96, 144 and 240 dpi. Not decided: whether the playable host (S7.5 / S8) should prefer an integer scale with black bars, or a filtered scale; both keep input_map's Viewport contract (fit_viewport supplies origin and content size).
path to resolution: Mariano's playtest (S7.5) decides the look; fit_viewport / Presenter::render are the only places to change.

description: [S7.3, kind `scope`] WM_DPICHANGED (a window dragged to a monitor of another dpi) resizes the client to the new dpi and refits the Viewport, but no test drives it: the PC has one monitor (240 dpi) and the tests set the dpi with --dpi, which takes the same sizing function (AppWindow::size_for_dpi) without the message.
path to resolution: A second monitor, or a test that sends WM_DPICHANGED with a suggested rect to the window and checks the new client size and a click's logical point.

description: [S7.3, kind `scope`] The client capture (app_drive.py App.capture) BitBlts the window DC, i.e. DWM's redirection surface; the tests ran with the window shown (SW_SHOWNOACTIVATE) on screen. A minimised or off-screen window is not covered, and a capture taken before the first WM_PAINT after the frame would show the black start frame (the app prints READY only after UpdateWindow has painted the frame).
path to resolution: Repeat the window tests with the window moved off-screen and minimised; if a capture differs, render through PrintWindow(PW_RENDERFULLCONTENT) in the driver.

description: [S7.3, kind `scope`] RealClock::idle_until sleeps in MsgWaitForMultipleObjects until the next instant the wait loop needs, where the original busy-calls pumpInput483c30 between clock reads (waitTicks 0x0045bfc1). time_model.md section 7 measures that no input is dispatched inside the H1 wait in the corpus, so the sleep changes no simulation input there; a message arriving during the wait wakes the sleep, and what S7.6's pump does with it then is S7.6's (its CPU < 5 % gate).
path to resolution: S7.6: dispatch the woken pump through the live core's InputSource and check against a recording with input posted inside a frame wait.

description: [S7.3, kind `value`] Measured frame period of frame_wait on RealClock with no work: 20 frames, min 91, max 95, mean 93.2 ms (timeBeginPeriod 1, this PC, idle), i.e. 87 ms plus one waitTicks quantum of 10 ms minus the part of the quantum before the deadline, as time_model.md section 3 predicts. Not measured under in-game load or with other processes busy.
path to resolution: S7.6 (over >= 300 live frames) and S7.5 (in-game load).

description: [S7.3, kind `scope`] The saves overlay hides a deleted install file with a tombstone in <data>/deleted.lst; the original's load browser deletes the file from the install's Saved Games folder itself (menu.cpp / saveload.cpp call GameFiles::remove). Deleting deleted.lst brings the install's copy back. No corpus segment or test deletes an install save through the app yet.
path to resolution: A scenario that deletes a save in the load browser run through the app (S7.4 recordings), checking the listing before and after.
